title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: OCR scanning of images on Windows devices (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents that Syntex pay-as-you-go licensing is not yet available in GCC, rather than leaving government-cloud billing wholly unstated. The briefing also omits required Azure permissions and Windows updates, and describes a rolling bandwidth window as a daily reset. The roadmap facts and the three portal routes are supported.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The item plans OCR detection of sensitive image content and DLP enforcement against exfiltration on Windows endpoint devices.
claims.quote: Optical character recognition (OCR) support will detect sensitive content in images and subsequently apply data loss prevention (DLP) policies to prevent exfiltration of that sensitive data on your Windows endpoint devices.

claims.claim: This roadmap release supports JPG, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP and image-only PDF.
claims.quote: This release supports key file types like JPG, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP and PDF (image only PDF).

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: OCR is admin-opt-in: it is optional and must be enabled at tenant level.
claims.quote: OCR scanning is an optional feature that you must enable at the tenant level.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The documented general OCR licensing model is consumption through Syntex pay-as-you-go billing in Azure.
claims.quote: Your Global or SharePoint admin must follow the instructions in Set up Microsoft Syntex billing in Azure to add a subscription for OCR.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Optical character recognition (OCR) reaches tenant OCR configuration for locations and groups.
claims.quote: Select Settings. Select Optical character recognition (OCR) to enter your OCR configuration settings. Select the locations where you want to scan images. Select the groups that you want included or excluded from OCR scans.
claims.fix: Keep the path, which reaches the correct configuration page, and add to its note: 'Select the locations to scan and the groups to include or exclude.'

claims.claim: No tenant OCR settings PowerShell, Graph or other API is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview tenant OCR settings PowerShell Graph API; "OCR" "Set-" "Compliance" "PowerShell". Read ocr-learn-about and Graph security-ocrsettings; returned automation concerns eDiscovery cases or supervisory review, not tenant DLP OCR.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > Advanced classification scanning and protection reaches the per-device cloud bandwidth settings.
claims.quote: To access these settings, from the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings. Advanced classification scanning and protection

claims.claim: No automation for the Endpoint DLP cloud classification bandwidth setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP settings PowerShell advanced classification bandwidth API; "Endpoint" "Set-DlpCompliancePolicy" "bandwidth". Read dlp-configure-endpoint-settings and searched Set-DlpCompliancePolicy reference; no bandwidth parameter found.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows reaches Windows DLP path exclusions.
claims.quote: To configure path exclusions in DLP settings, go to Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows.

claims.claim: No automation for Endpoint DLP Windows file path exclusions is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "file path exclusions" "PowerShell" "DLP"; Endpoint DLP settings API. Read dlp-configure-endpoint-settings and searched Set-DlpCompliancePolicy reference; results document portal exclusions, policy user scopes or antivirus exclusions, not this setting.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Existing DLP policies and sensitive-information-type conditions apply to text in images when OCR is configured.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview applies your existing policies for data loss prevention (DLP), records management, and insider risk management (IRM) to images and text-based content.

claims.claim: The general OCR page does not state cloud coverage or confirm its described design for GCC, GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview OCR Windows endpoint requirements GCC High DoD; OCR pay-as-you-go price GCC High DoD Microsoft Purview government. Read all of ocr-learn-about and the GCC High deployment table; neither confirms endpoint OCR cloud-specific design.

claims.claim: The GCC High planning table has no OCR row in its DLP section.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview OCR Windows endpoint GCC High DoD. Read the full GCC High deployment table: its DLP section has no OCR row; its OCR entry is under Communication Compliance.

claims.claim: The GCC High planning page warns that identified status is subject to change.
claims.quote: Identified status is subject to change as project plans and priorities are reevaluated.

claims.claim: Without OCR, text-based sensitive-information detection cannot read image-based documents or screenshots.
claims.quote: Without OCR, DLP policies, and auto-labeling policies can't scan image-based content, scanned documents, screenshots, and invoices, leaving sensitive data in images unprotected.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/zero-trust-purview-protect-data to sources for the statement about image-based content without OCR.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: OCR stops scanning images when the device bandwidth limit is reached, and the limit can be increased.
claims.quote: OCR stops scanning images once this daily limit is reached. If you want to continue scanning images, you can increase the bandwidth limit.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: After reaching the limit, OCR remains stopped until a daily reset or the administrator raises the limit.
claims.quote: When the cumulative bandwidth usage drops below the rolling 24-hour limit, communication with the cloud services resumes.
claims.fix: Replace 'until the limit resets or you raise it' and 'until you raise the limit or the daily limit resets' with 'until cumulative bandwidth usage drops below the rolling 24-hour limit or you increase the limit'.

claims.claim: OCR settings generally take effect about an hour after activation.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each scanned standalone image counts as one billable transaction.
claims.quote: Each image scanned counts as one transaction. This pricing means that stand-alone images (JPEG, JPG, PNG, BMP, or TIFF) each count as a single transaction.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each PDF page is charged separately.
claims.quote: It also means that each page in a PDF file is charged separately.

claims.claim: A 10-page PDF scan counts as 10 separate scans.
claims.quote: For example, if there are 10 pages in a PDF file, an OCR scan of the PDF file counts as 10 separate scans.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 pay-as-you-go pricing page lists OCR at $0.001 per transaction.
claims.quote: $0.001/transaction

claims.claim: A scanned image may be used in any number of DLP, insider risk, auto-labeling and records management policies without extra charge.
claims.quote: Additionally, you can use each scanned image in any number of policies across data loss prevention, insider risk management, auto-labeling, and records management at no extra charge.

claims.claim: Endpoint OCR caching is maintained for 30 days to reduce costs.
claims.quote: To reduce your OCR costs, the service uses the following caching mechanisms: ... For Endpoint, the cache is maintained for 30 days.

claims.claim: The Endpoint OCR cache is local to each device.
claims.quote: Caching is local to each endpoint device and only classifiers identified on the image and image hash are stored.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout

claims.fix: Qualify the Endpoint estimator instruction with: 'For Endpoint, first install the latest Windows Update released on February 29, 2024 or later.' Retain the preview label and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ocr-cost-estimator.
